Revenue trajectory: FY24 +0.4%, FY25 +3.1%, FY26 ~+10.8% → 🟢 Accelerating (strong surge from flat prior years) EPS trajectory: FY24 −14.1%, FY25 +3.5%, FY26 ~+16% → 🟢 Accelerating (recovering from FY24 trough)

Acceleration flags:

  • Rev: RNS midpoint £790m → +10.8% vs prior +3.1% → acceleration ✓ (RNS-derived)
  • EPS: Midpoint ~160p → +16% vs prior +3.5% → acceleration ✓ (RNS-derived)

3.2 Seasonal H1 % of FY Baseline, Tracking Deviation and Signal (pre-FY mode — write but do not score)

H1 FY26 actual = £365.6m. FY26 guidance midpoint £790m. H1 as % of FY26 = £365.6m / £790m = 46.3% vs 3yr avg 48.7% → deviation = −2.4pp

Signal (informational): 🔴 CAUTION (−1.5 to −3pp). H1 slightly below seasonal norm — but RNS has upgraded FY guidance, meaning H2 must be stronger. This is consistent with the strong demand acceleration noted post-H1 results.

EPS H1 tracking (informational): H1 EPS 68.8p / FY26e 156.5p = 44.0% vs 48.7% → deviation = −4.7pp. Below seasonal norm. But: FY26 EPS will upgrade from 156.5p to ~160p. Recalculated: 68.8p / 160p = 43.0% → deviation = −5.7pp. H1 EPS below seasonal, H2 must compensate.

Phase 3.2 not scored (pre-FY mode). Column 5: na.

3.3 Implied H2 Momentum vs Historical (pre-FY mode — scored in Phase 5)

H2 base figure (RNS-derived midpoint): FY26 midpoint £790m − H1 £365.6m = £424.4m H2 range: Floor £775m − £365.6m = £409.4m · Ceiling £805m − £365.6m = £439.4m Prior H2 FY25 = £371.6m H2 YoY: midpoint = (£424.4m − £371.6m) / £371.6m = +14.2%

Classification: 🟢 strong (+14.2% YoY, above +10% threshold). RNS-derived.

EPS H2: PBT midpoint £155m → FY26 EPS ~160p. H2 EPS = ~160p − 68.8p = ~91.2p vs FY25 H2 74.6p → +22.3% YoY. 🟢 strong.

Phase 3.3 scored row: pre-FY mode → included in Phase 5. 🟢 strong.

3.4 Forecast Broker Momentum Overlay

  • EPS net +19.8% over full period (130.6p → 156.5p). Very large step-up in Sep 25 (+24.6p — possibly post-FY25 results upgrade). Since then modest further upgrades. 4-week trend: 🔴 FALLING (very slightly, 157.2p → 156.5p — likely pre-announcement drift/caution). Post-RNS this trend will reverse sharply.
  • Divergence: Price rallied from £31.64 → £40.68 (+28.6%) alongside EPS +19.8% — broadly aligned, no major divergence. Both rising together.

3.5 Balance Sheet & Debt Profile

Reporting currency: GBP

RNS-vs-forecast reconciliation: RNS confirms strong demand and order book expansion. No explicit cash figure in this statement. Sharescope FY1fc net borrowing = −£276.3m (very large net cash vs H1 current −£63.4m). This large H1-to-FY step in net cash (−£63.4m → −£276.3m) in Sharescope seems anomalous. Likely reflecting expected large H2 cash generation — RSW has historically strong H2 free cash flow, consistent with high H2 revenue weighting. No RNS cash disclosure to verify. Note gap as informational — cannot reconcile without RNS cash figure.

ND/EBITDA: FY1fc −1.70x (net cash, substantial). Interest cover: negative (net cash). ND/FCF −4.6x. Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash — Phase 5 silent.

Forecast year earnings check:

  • Step 1: FY1fc EPS 156.5p → upgrading to ~160p. FY25 actual 137.8p → growing +16%. Revenue £759.3m (consensus pre-RNS) → actual ~£790m > FY25 £713.0m → ✅✅ growing +10.8%.
  • Step 2: FY2fc EPS 174.6p > FY1fc 156.5p → ✅✅ growing +11.5%. Revenue £801.9m > £759.3m → ✅✅ growing. Post-upgrade FY27e likely further enhanced.

3.6 Structural / One-off Flags

  • Semiconductor and electronics demand surge: Structural demand driver — AI infrastructure buildout driving semiconductor equipment capex globally. Renishaw's precision measurement tools are directly in the supply chain. Not a one-off.
  • Aerospace & defence: UK/European defence spending step-up a multi-year structural tailwind.
  • Supply chain and cost pressures: Explicitly flagged by management — geopolitical uncertainty and supply chain costs are headwinds that partially offset the demand surge.
  • Order book expansion — "substantial": Strong signal for FY27 revenue visibility.

PHASE 4 — BROKER-REACTION SIMULATION

RSW · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/6/26

#1 Driver — Explicit FY26 guidance upgrade: Revenue range £775–805m (+2–6% vs £759.3m consensus). PBT range £145–165m (floor to +14% vs £145m consensus). The headline "Upgrade to FY2026 guidance" is unambiguous. Brokers will upgrade FY26 estimates across the board.

#2 Driver — Order book expansion and sector demand: "Substantial expansion of our order book" in semiconductor/electronics and aerospace/defence. These are forward-looking revenue signals that support FY27 upgrades beyond the FY26 raise.

Forecast revisions:

  • FY1 Revenue (FY26e): Upgrade from £759.3m to midpoint ~£790m. +4.0%.
  • FY1 PBT (FY26e): Upgrade from £145.0m. Midpoint £155m = +6.9%. Brokers likely model toward midpoint-to-upper range.
  • FY1 EPS (FY26e): Upgrade from 156.5p to approximately 160–165p (+2–5%).
  • FY2 Revenue (FY27e): Upgrade, supported by order book. £801.9m → ~£820–840m. +2–5%.
  • FY2 EPS (FY27e): Upgrade from 174.6p to ~180–190p. +3–9%.
  • Target price: Current TP £40.03, share price £40.68. Price is already above TP — brokers have not caught up. Post-upgrade TPs likely move to £44–48. Re-rating potential.

Conservative guidance read-through: Range guidance with both metrics provided — not cautious language. Titled "Upgrade to FY2026 guidance" — no ambiguity.

Key risk: Supply chain pressures and cost inflation could compress the PBT range toward the £145m floor rather than the £155–165m midpoint-to-upper range. If the FX headwind materialises meaningfully (Renishaw has significant international revenue), net revenue in GBP could be impacted. The fact that price is already above TP suggests the market partially anticipates the upgrade — upside may be partially priced.

Net FY1 EPS revision: upgrade (+2–5%). Consistency check: Tone Constructive or Strongly positive. Given explicit "Upgrade" language with dual metric ranges → Strongly positive. ✅

Overall tone: 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

PHASE 5 — FINAL SCORE & VERDICT

RSW · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 30/6/26

77/100 · Confidence: 72–82 · No FX badge (no Phase 0B trigger from available data) · 🟢🟢 Strongly positive / upgrade cycle starting

ComponentPts
🟢 Explicit FY26 guidance upgrade — revenue £775–805m vs £759.3m consensus (+2–6%)+15
🟢 PBT upgrade range £145–165m — midpoint £155m = +6.9% vs £145m consensus+12
🟢 H2 FY26 implied revenue +14.2% YoY (midpoint) — H2 surge confirming demand acceleration+10
🟢 Semiconductor + aerospace/defence structural demand — order book "substantially expanded"+9
🟢 EPS trajectory accelerating — FY24 −14%, FY25 +3.5%, FY26 ~+16%+8
🟢 Net cash >£276m FY1fc — balance sheet supports further growth investment+5
🟡 Supply chain and cost pressures explicitly flagged — may compress toward PBT range floor−3
🟡 4-week EPS trend FALLING into announcement — partial pricing-in risk−2
🔴 PBT range floor (£145m) = in-line with stale consensus — downside risk if cost headwinds bite−5
🔴 FY27e revenue growth only +1.5% stale consensus — forward year growth slowdown−4
🔴 Share price already above consensus TP £40.03 (close £40.68) — market partially priced upgrade−3
🔴 H1 FY26 revenue at 46.3% of FY guidance midpoint — slightly below seasonal norm (H2 heavy)−2

Total: 77/100

Para 1 — Headline numbers: The headline says it all: "Upgrade to FY2026 guidance." Revenue guidance of £775m–£805m (midpoint £790m) is above the pre-RNS consensus of £759.3m by +4.0% at the midpoint, with the ceiling implying +6.0%. Adjusted PBT of £145m–£165m raises the earnings bar from the stale consensus floor of £145m to a midpoint of £155m, representing a +6.9% upgrade at mid-range. The underlying driver is crystal clear: "particularly strong demand from customers in the semiconductor and electronics manufacturing equipment, and aerospace & defence sectors" combined with a "further substantial expansion of our order book" — both structural tailwinds tied to AI infrastructure buildout and European defence spending escalation.

Para 2 — H2 momentum & upgrade resilience: Pre-FY mode. H2 FY26 implied revenue at the midpoint is approximately £424m, representing +14.2% YoY versus FY25's £371.6m — the strongest H2 in the company's recent history. H2 EPS implied at approximately 91p versus FY25's 74.6p represents +22.3% YoY growth. The bear case rests on cost headwinds: management explicitly flags "increasing costs imposed by ongoing economic and geopolitical uncertainties and supply chain pressures" — if these compress margins toward the PBT floor of £145m, EPS remains flat vs stale consensus rather than upgrading. However, the order book expansion provides a buffer: even at the floor, revenue remains significantly above consensus.

Para 3 — Broker revisions & verdict: FY26e revenue will be upgraded from £759.3m to approximately £790m (+4.0%), and FY26e EPS from 156.5p to ~160–165p (+2–5%). FY27e receives a secondary lift to approximately £820–840m revenue and 180–190p EPS (+3–9%) supported by order book visibility. Target prices are expected to move to £44–48 from the stale £40.03 consensus — the current price at £40.68 is already through the old TP, creating a re-rating scenario. The primary watch point is cost management: brokers will focus on the PBT range width (£145–165m, a £20m spread) and whether supply chain disruptions push toward the floor.

🏁 RSW delivers an explicit, unambiguous FY26 guidance upgrade driven by structural semiconductor and defence demand, with strong H2 momentum and order book expansion underpinning a genuine upgrade cycle. Score: 77/100.

SUP

Routing mode: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update / FY guidance update accordingly. Next year end = 31/3/26 → FY1 = FY26 · prior year = FY25 · FY2 = FY27. Sharescope data reflects the pre-RNS state.

Year label mappings:

  • FY23 = 3y ago · FY24 = 2y ago · FY25 = 1y ago · FY26e = FY1 (1y fc) · FY27e = FY2 (2y fc)

PHASE 1 — DATA CONTEXT

SUP · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

  • Routing: pre-FY (latest qtrly report = 'Q2'). Interpreting incoming RNS as pre-FY trading update accordingly.
  • FY1 consensus (FY26e): EPS 18.4p · Revenue £245.7m
  • FY2 consensus (FY27e): EPS 20.5p · Revenue £290.4m
  • Forecast broker momentum: EPS net change over full period −17.5% (22.3p → 18.4p). Material downgrade cycle in Jul 25 (22.3→17.9p, -4.4p event). Partial recovery Oct 25 (17.9→18.4p). Then flat from Oct 25 to Apr 26 — stalled at 18.4p for six months. Revenue: £235.1m → £245.7m (+4.5%). 4-week trend: 🟡 FLAT
  • H1 baselines (3yr avg): Revenue 46.0% of FY = £113.1m · EPS 42.9% of FY = 7.9p
  • Prior-year H1 actuals (FY25): Revenue £113.0m · EPS 10.8p
  • Implied H2 YoY (pre-FY mode): H1 FY26 actual = £132.6m (per Sharescope current H1). H2 implied = FY26e £245.7m − £132.6m = £113.1m. Prior H2 FY25 = £118.1m. Implied H2 YoY = £113.1m − £118.1m = −4.2%. EPS: FY26e 18.4p − H1 actual 8.8p = H2 implied 9.6p vs FY25 H2 = 10.2p → −5.9%
  • FX: Currency = GBP. No FX exposure. Phase 0B N/A.
  • Reporting currency & debt: GBP · Net debt: FY25 H2 £0.5m → FY26 H1 £19.9m (net debt) → FY1fc £7.3m → FY2fc £1.1m. ND/EBITDA FY1fc 0.20x. Interest cover 23.2x. ND/FCF 0.6x. Debt flag: 🟢 Unlevered / net cash (essentially).

PHASE 2 — RNS EXTRACTION & QUANTIFICATION

SUP · Q2 · Pre-FY Trading Update · FY26 · Year end: 31/3/26

RNS type: Pre-FY Trading Update (FY26 — twelve months ended 31 March 2026)

  1. Revenue — FY26 actual: "expects to report a 15% increase in FY26 revenues of c.£265.0 million (FY25: £231.1 million)." vs FY26e consensus £245.7m → beat of £19.3m = +7.9%.

"The Company expects to report a 15% increase in FY26 revenues of c.£265.0 million (FY25: £231.1 million)"

  1. EBITDA — FY26 actual: "Adjusted EBITDA of approximately £40.6 million (FY25: £40.5 million), significantly ahead of market consensus expectations." vs consensus £37.0m → beat of £3.6m = +9.7%. EBITDA margin: £40.6m/£265.0m = 15.3% vs FY25 £40.5m/£231.1m = 17.5%. Margin compression of 2.2pp despite revenue growth — driven by acquisition costs and investment in new facilities.

"Adjusted EBITDA of approximately £40.6 million (FY25: £40.5 million), significantly ahead of market consensus expectations"

  1. EPS bridge (FY27e):
  • New base: FY26 EBITDA £40.6m. Finance costs: net cash ~£7.3m FY26. Interest income likely positive. Capex £5.0m. Tax ~25%. Adj PBT ~ EBITDA − D&A − interest cost. Working: EBITDA £40.6m, D&A estimated ~£3–4m (from asset base), interest net ~nil, PBT ~£37m, tax ~£9.25m, PAT ~£27.75m, shares ~117.3m → EPS ~23.7p (basic). But wait — Sharescope FY26e EPS is only 18.4p on consensus, implying significant adjustments. The company uses "Adjusted EBITDA" which excludes share-based payments, fair value movements, exceptional items. Statutory EPS will be lower. Using 18.4p consensus as adjusted EPS benchmark.
  • EPS bridge: FY26 actual adj EBITDA = £40.6m vs consensus £37.0m → +£3.6m upside. FY27e drivers: SlimFast (acquired during FY26) full year contribution; new manufacturing facilities operational; vaping resilience continues. Vaping +10%+ despite ban confirms structural resilience.
  • Organic EBITDA growth: FY26 £40.6m achieved despite acquisitions of £12.4m (SlimFast etc.) and £5.0m capex. FY27 benefit from full-year SlimFast + margin normalisation as acquisition costs fall away.
  • 🏗️ Investment step-up: "investment in two brand new manufacturing facilities." New wellness facility 40,000 sq ft. RNS states "positioned for long-term growth" — cost timing in FY26/FY27. FY26 capex £5.0m confirmed (matches Sharescope fc). FY27 ongoing running costs from new facilities = mild negative. Score as FY+1 consideration.
  • FY27e EPS bridge: FY26 consensus 18.4p will upgrade to ~20–22p on EBITDA beat alone (+9.7%). FY27e 20.5p (current) will be revised to ~22–24p on SlimFast full year + margin recovery. Implied FY27e EPS upgrade +7–17% vs stale 20.5p.
  1. Vaping: "expected to be more than 10% higher than prior year even with the UK disposable vape ban on 1 June 2025." This directly addresses the key bear case — ban proved manageable. Demonstrates market resilience and category strength.

"Sales from the Group's Vaping category are expected to be more than 10% higher than prior year even with the UK disposable vape ban on 1 June 2025"

  1. Drinks & Wellness / SlimFast: "boosted by an excellent contribution from SlimFast." SlimFast acquired during FY26, no full-year contribution in FY26 → FY27 gets full year.
  2. Capital returns / Balance sheet: After £12.4m acquisitions + £5.0m capex, "the Group remains net-cash positive at 31 March 2026." Robust balance sheet. RNS-vs-forecast reconciliation: RNS net cash positive vs Sharescope FY1fc net debt £7.3m (positive = debt). RNS explicitly says net-cash positive — variance vs Sharescope.
